messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool "cerulean-123" (CeruleanLabs) GPU util >=98% for 12m, queue length 520, pending tokens 1.2M. Severity: page.

emma (oncall): ack. looking...

raj (eng-sre): jumping in — pulling pool metrics. gpu_util 98-100 across all 8 nodes, avg queue latency 2.1s, 95th token latency 3.2s. logs show sustained long requests from customer tenant 'cerulean'.

emma (oncall): customer impact? jane (cs) any inbound pings?

jane (cs): just got a DM from Cerulean on runbooks, they report errors and timeouts in production. confirmed they’re on Dedicated (VPC) with reserved 8 GPUs, they rely on low latency. They signed burst policy but need approval for cross-tenant burst into shared pool.

lee (eng-platform): note: their pool is soft-limited by tenant quota; autoscale is disabled for this pool (org policy) — to burst we'd need explicit override (ops approval) and to gate to compatible model variants.

sara (prod-sre): options: 1) activate emergency burst to shared pooled capacity for 30m (high cost, preserves latency), 2) shed lower-priority Cerulean jobs (batch vs sync) keeping critical paths, 3) fallback to smaller quantized model (quality regressions), 4) route to degraded capacity with increased timeouts.

emma (oncall): what's current backlog by priority? raj?

raj (eng-sre): backlog: sync requests 420, batch 100. Sync requests dominate 90% of tokens. No other tenants in their dedicated pool.

emma (oncall): they are single-tenant pool => option 2 not possible. We need to decide between short burst or model fallback.

jane (cs): Cerulean prefers no quality change. They approve short burst if we sign SLA credit? I'm drafting message. They gave green light for 30m burst with cost backfill.

lee (eng-platform): quick safety check: can we spin up 2x g5 nodes in shared pool in region eu-west-1 within 3-5m? quota available but needs burst flag.

ops-bot: quota-check: spare GPUs in shared pool in eu-west-1 = 6. Provision time estimate 4m.

emma (oncall): @raj @lee go ahead with 30m emergency burst. execute runbook step: emergency-burst -> attach shared nodes and only accept Cerulean's sync requests on attached nodes, enable preemption for non-critical workloads.

raj (eng-sre): running command:
```bash
rbctl pool burst --pool-id=cerulean-123 --region=eu-west-1 --nodes=2 --duration=30m --restrict-to-tenant=cerulean --preempt-policy=noncritical
```

ops-bot: Action started: provisioning 2 nodes. Estimated ready at +4m.

sara (prod-sre): I'll monitor queue and token latency; set SLO alert to quiet until stabilization. Also prepare rollback: if no reduction in queue length within 7m, we fallback to model-quant1.

emma (oncall): CS update to customer: "We are provisioning short-term capacity (30m) to restore latency. We'll follow up with postmortem and options to increase long-term capacity." (sending now)

jane (cs): sent to Cerulean: they ack and requested notification once burst completes. They asked for root cause analysis and long-term capacity plan.

ops-bot: Provision complete: 2 nodes attached. Pool util dropping: avg gpu_util 78% -> queue length 110 -> token latency 0.6s.

raj (eng-sre): confirming traffic is draining. No errors introduced.

emma (oncall): great. set incident status: mitigated. will keep monitoring for 30m and then remove burst unless we agree on extension. @jane please coordinate follow-up meeting with Cerulean.

jane (cs): will schedule. sending brief to AE and customer execs.

sara (prod-sre): handoff to night oncall in 25m. leaving notes in incident doc: cause = unexpected spike in sync workload, mitigation = temporary burst to shared pool; next steps = capacity planning + optional model fallback if cost unacceptable.

emma (oncall): closing active paging. thanks all. :tada:
